text: Lulu is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found at Seoris Plaza in the Indoline Praetorium. Lulu offers no quests or merc missions.

Lost & Found (Japanese: , Sagashimono wa Otoshimono) is a quest in . It can be received from Pororo on the plateau beyond the Skybridge on the Bionis' Shoulder. Pororo offers rewards upon progression in collecting her Favourites. After completing the quest, Pororo moves to Gran Dell.
Lott is a Homs in . and can be found in Gran Dell on the Bionis' Shoulder and gives the quest Finding Happiness.
Loh'ban is a High Entia in . He can be found at Companions' Cape and later in Gran Dell on the Bionis' Shoulder during the day.

Lost in a Dark Dream is a Time Attack challenge in . It can be received from the Nopon Archsage. The challenge battle is located on the Bionis' Shoulder, and it is unlocked after clearing the main story of .
M100 Helms L are heavy head armour in . They can be purchased from Time Attack for 4,860 Noponstones.
M100 Plates L are heavy torso armour in . They can be purchased from Time Attack for 9,720 Noponstones.
M100 Arms L are heavy arms armour in . They can be purchased from Time Attack for 3,850 Noponstones.
M100 Cuisses L are heavy legs armour in . They can be purchased from Time Attack for 7,770 Noponstones.
M100 Greaves L are heavy feet armour in . They can be purchased from Time Attack for 5,850 Noponstones.

Lora's Charm-making is a skill in , with which Lora can prepare Charm Pouch items from various Collectibles at campsites. These recipes and items are unique to Lora and cannot be obtained any other way. Recipes are unlocked by receiving them as rewards for certain Quests. Lora is the only character who can craft Charms.
Literacy Beatdown (Japanese: ) is Adenine's Level IV Blade Special in .
Lumian was the forty-seventh Emperor of the High Entia, centuries prior to the events of Xenoblade Chronicles.
Luca's Eyot (Japanese: , Ruka no Kyokushū) is a Landmark in , located on Viliera Hill in Millick Meadows.
Lone Exile (Japanese: , Rōn Eguzairu) is a Kevesi Defender class in .
Limits Unbound (Japanese: ) is Noah's Ouroboros Chain Art in .
Lost Vanguard (Japanese: , Rosuto Vangādo) is an Agnian Defender class in .

Low Maktha Wildwood (Japanese: , Morukuna Daishinrin: Kasō) is a Area in . It is located in the Pentelas Region. It is the lower level of Maktha Wildwood and is filled with higher level enemies, including a Superboss.

Loska's Cavern (Japanese: , Rosuka Dōkutsu) is a Location in . It is located on the Urayan Trail. It leads to Loska Plateau, where Colony 5 is located. Most of the cavern is blocked off until Side Story: Eunie.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Long-Range Memories are Accessories in . The common variant can be purchased from the Clifftop Caravan, and the legendary variant can be obtained from Altruistic Maribel.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Luminous Memories are Accessories in . The legendary variant can be obtained from Turbulent Martinez.
Loch Ciel (Japanese: , Shieru Kosui) is a Landmark in , located on Melnath's Shoulder.

The Llyn Nyddwr Camp (Japanese: , Neusu-ko no Kyūsokuchi) is a Rest Spot in . It is located at Llyn Nyddwr in Ribbi Flats. The Lakeside Caravan is located here. If the Expansion Pass has been purchased and Challenge Battles! has been accepted, a portal will appear here that grants access to the Land of Challenge. After downloading the Version 2.1.0 update, Miibomii can be found here. Talking to her after completing the game and meeting certain conditions unlocks weapon skins of Pyra and Mythra's Aegis Swords for the Swordfighter class if their respective amiibo have not been used. After downloading the Version 2.2.0 update, talking to Miibomii after meeting certain conditions unlocks outfits
The Lost Colony Barracks (Japanese: , Bōkyaku no Koronī Heisha) is a Rest Spot in . It is located within the Lost Colony of Erythia Sea.

Loska Plateau (Japanese: , Rosuka Daichi) is a Location in . It is located beyond Loska's Cavern on the Urayan Trail. Colony 5 is located here, with its Ferronis being located toward the end of the plateau.

Littlefort Morley (Japanese: , Ogi no Mōrī) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Pagul family, and can be found at level 46 near Needle Reef Beach in Erythia Sea. The Cavalry Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
The Lower Drainage (Japanese: , Teisō Haisuiro) is a Location in . It is located in the Castle Drainage of Keves Castle, accessible from the Throne Room.
Limoux Hill (Japanese: , Rimū no Oka) is a Location in . It is located in the Dannagh Desert in the Fornis Region.
Luscious Fillets are Key Items in . They are dropped by Eregaa Anloods, and three are required to complete Stolen Provisions.
Llyn Nyddwr (Japanese: , Neusu-ko, Lake Neus) is a Location in , located in Ribbi Flats. The Llyn Nyddwr Camp Rest Spot can be found here.
Lisza Garden (Japanese: , Rīza no Sono) is a Location in . It is located on Rae-Bel Tableland in the Fornis Region.
Lucifurnaces are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be produced by the Tableland Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Longleaves are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be produced by the Tableland Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

|-|XC3 = |-|FR = Limelightstones are Ore Collectible items in and . They can be found in the Fornis Region in . They can also be produced from the Desert Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They can be found on the Aurora Shelf in .
Limber Ladies are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be produced from the Desert Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Loloka is a Nopon NPC in . Loloka can be found at the Old Way Camp at the Old Cliffside Way.
Lodmoro Plambuses are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Plambus family, and can be found at level 73-74 at Low Maktha Wildwood. __TOC__
Lozenge Diamonds are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Keves Castle Region. They can also be produced from the Perimeter Outlet Fabricator after the first step of Colony 0 renovation.
Lively Quartz are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Atoll Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Lucent Ambers are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Sandbar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Lunar Rails are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Origin. They can also be produced from the Cascade Ferronis Hulk Fabricator after reaching Origin for the first time.
Lucky Marrin Thickcuts are items in . They are dropped by Marrins. The Maroking Marrin also drops them during Happiness, with one being needed for the quest.
Lucky Seven, also known as the Sword of The End and the Sword of Origin (Japanese: ) is a special Blade in and .
Little Aries are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Aries family, and can be found at level 87-88 in The Cavity of Swordmarch.
Lods Torays are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are Droids, and can be found at level 62-63 at Amplifier No. 1, Amplifier No. 2, and the Amplifier Section in the Origin Interior.
Lods Zetorays are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are Droids, and can be found at level 63-64 at Amplifier No. 1, Amplifier No. 2, and the Amplifier Section in the Origin Interior.
Lotus (Japanese: , Renge) is a NPC in . Lotus is from Colony Mu.
Lomi Hill (Japanese: , Romi no Oka) is a Location in . It is located on Rae-Bel Tableland in the Fornis Region.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Lustrous Armrings are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the O'Virbus Commissary and Handypon, and the legendary variant can be obtained from Saberly Dorampé.
Lognate Darbuses are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Darbus family, and can be found at level 50 in the Eagus Wilderness.

Little Armus are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Armu family, and can be found at level 19-20 in Rae-Bel Tableland. Four are also fought at level 50 during the first wave of the Challenge Battle Pretty Fierce.
Luina Volffs are Quest Exclusive Bosses in . They are members of the Volff family, and five are fought at level 33 in High Maktha Wildwood during Off-Seeing Customs.
Lurking Spider (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is one of Taion's Ouroboros arts.
Lustrous Spike is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Noponic Champion class. It becomes a usable Master Art upon unlocking the class.
Lost Advent (Japanese: , Rosuto Adobento) is a Chain Art in . It is Monica's Chain Art during a Chain Attack.

Luminous Illusion (Japanese: , Ruminasuiryūjon) is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Aerial Slash used only by Alexandria. She does an upward slash, then a slash to the left, then downwards to the right and finishes with a backwards flipping slash.
This is a list of pre-release and unused content for the game and .

The Lucky Seven License is a DLC Key Item in . It can be bought from the Prize X-change Blue for 60,000 blue Noponstone. It allows Noah to use Infinity Blade and Unlimited Sword as his Talent Art on the hard difficulty during the Archsage's Gauntlet.

The Lumos Garrison (Japanese: , Ruminaria Chūryūchi) is a location in , located near the Lumos Pillar Remnants on The Ragmos Desolation. It is made up of the remnants of the Lumos Pedestal area. It is an Agnus Outpost occupied by Agnus Forces. The Garrison Key found here is required to open the garrison's gate.

Lucille is an NPC in . She is the older sister of Hamill, and a member of the Liberators in Colony 9. Lucille's Community is gained when talking to her after completing The Running Automaton, starting Chapter 4, changing Hamill's Community status, and talking to her three times.

The Lumos Pillar Remnants (Japanese: , Ruminaria Shichū Iseki) is a Location in . It is located on The Ragmos Desolation. It is the remnants of the Lumos Pedestal from the Kingdom of Tantal. An Affinity Scene can be viewed here. There is also a Relic found here.
Longhorn Ignas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 35 at the Declessa Cave Temple Ruins on the Aurora Shelf.
Logos (Japanese: , Rogosu) was one of three units of the Trinity Processor in the .
Luminescent Laia Fins are items in . They can be dropped by Dark Laias on the Aurora Shelf.

Lost Days of Warmth is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track seven of disc one from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track seven of disc twelve from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * During the Chapter 1 flashback of the aftermath of Noah, Lanz, Eunie, and Joran's loss in the mock battle against Garvel's squad. * The party considers whether to travel through the Eagus Wilderness or Elaice Highway. * Sena expressing his desire to Mio about pulling her own weight for the party during Chapter 3. * When Taion gives Eunie tea to help calm her. * When Taion tells Noah and Mio about Nimue's pocket watch. * When

Certain mechanics in required an Online connection. All of these mechanics are now discontinued due to two events. On November 7/8th, 2017, the Miiverse social network shut down, preventing the BLADE Report messaging system from being accessible. On April 8th, 2024, the Wii U Online Services ceased operations. Along with it, all of the remaining Online features in ended as well, which resulted in many items and Achievements becoming unobtainable, as well as some mechanics left unable to be experienced. The following is a list of Achievements, Armor, Weapons, Holofigures, Materials, and mechanics affected by the shutdown. Most of these mechanics returned in .
The Locket is an Important Item in . It is collected at Aaroy Plain in Oblivia during the course of Lost Memento.
Lummie is an NPC in . She is a Gormotti who can be found near the Waypoint Market in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya after reaching Merc Level 2.

Makna Path (Japanese: , Makuna no Rindō) is a landmark in . It is the first location in Makna Forest, as it is the entrance from the Bionis' Interior. It leads to the Agni Tablet, and is almost unpopulated by enemies. There is only a Makna Eluca and a few Apis, at the end of the path near the Tablet.
The Makna Forest Collection is a portion of the Collectopaedia in .
This page is a list of all the Unique Monsters in Makna Forest.
Marcia (Japanese: , Māsha) is a Homs in . She can be found in the western portion of the Commercial District of Colony 9.

Maker Bunnits (Japanese: , Meikā Banitto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Bunnit family. They are usually found north of the Jabos Rock Rest Area Landmark. Three of them need to be defeated to complete Bionis' Leg's Monster Quest 1 - Part 2.

Magnificent Digalus (Japanese: , Gōjū no Digariusu) is a Unique Monster in . It is the strongest Sauros and appears at level 99 in the vicinity of the Decayed Forest in Makna Forest after completing Mechonis Core.

Makna Elucas (Japanese: , Makuna Erūka) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Eluca family, and can be found at level 28 in the Yellow Flower Grove and Agni Tablet in Makna Forest. In the Yellow Flower Grove, they will dig out from the ground when a flower patch is approached. Five of them must be defeated for the quest Disinsectization. Additionally, they can drop the Green Eluca Juice needed for A Worried Bug-Lover.

Makna Eks are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Eks family, and can be found at level 33 near the Eks Watering Hole in Makna Forest. Defeating three of them is required to complete the quest Monster Quest 4. They can drop the Eks Iron Hearts needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction and The Melody of Happiness.
The Machina (English dub: ) are a race in . They are mechanical life inhabiting the Mechonis.

Ma'crish (Japanese: , Myukishiria) is a High Entia NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found in Alcamoth on the south side of the pond north of the shop. If she has not been invited to Colony 6, she can be found at the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg after the events at the Mechonis Core. In Colony 6, she leaves a house in front of the Reconstruction HQ at 6:00. She then talks around the Reconstruction HQ court until 9:00. She then moves to Hoko's food stand.

Macro Passions (Japanese: , Makuro Passhon) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in the High Entia Tomb. According to their description, Sharla named them on instinct and they are passionate balls of red thread.
Making Camp (Japanese: , Yaei no Junbi) is a quest in . It can be received from Bokoko in the Nopon Merchant Camp in Satorl Marsh. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

Making a Mixer (Japanese: , Mikisā Seisaku) is a quest in . It can be received from Rono in the Pollen Works in Frontier Village. Shulk must be in the lead and will comment. Once Making a Mixer is accepted, Materials for a Mixer is automatically triggered.

Marine Marbles (Japanese: , Marin Māburu) are collectables in . They can be found in the Eryth Sea. According to their description, they are blue stones that hold the essence of Eryth Sea and they are smooth and rare. Two are required for the Timed Quest Building Bridges.

Mane Cats (Japanese: , Tategamineko) are collectables in . They can be found in Eryth Sea. In , they can be found in Alcamoth. According to their description, they are very regal-looking cats and they have lovely smooth paw-pads.
Makna Caps (Japanese: , Makuna Kyappu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be bought with 1 slot from the Frontier Village Armour Shop for 3,840 G.
Makna Tops are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by various enemies, or bought at the Frontier Village Armour Shop.

The Mag Mell Ruins (Japanese: , Magu Merudo no Iseki) (English dub: ) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of Tephra Cave. Shulk, Reyn, and Fiora pass through here when they are going to collect the Ether Cylinders, and Shulk and Reyn pass through again on their way to Bionis' Leg. Defence Force soldiers can be found inside. In a short story included in Xenoblade: The Secret File it is revealed to be part of an ancient Alcamoth trading ship used for transporting Ether Cylinders. It is also a training ground for the Defence Force.
The Main Entrance (Japanese: , Koronī 9 Shōmen Kuchi) is a landmark in . It is located in Colony 9. As its name implies, it is the main entrance to Colony 9. It leads into the Commercial District.

This quest will expire if Colony 6 Reconstruction reaches 100%. Making a New Path (Japanese: , Ukai Rūto wo Tsukure) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Gorman in Reconstruction HQ in Colony 6, at the same time as For the Restoration is accepted. If this quest is completed before For the Restoration, a new path will be opened at Spiral Valley, making it possible to complete For the Restoration without defeating the monster blocking the path.

Makna Ansels are enemies in . They are members of the Ansel family, and can be found at level 32-34 in Makna Forest, near water; alongside the river running from Great Makna Falls, the Eks Watering Hole, and the Clear Waterfall. They do not appear during rain. They can drop the Tasty Ansel Wings needed for Heropon's Spirit. Two Makna Ansels must be defeated for the Makna Forest quest Monster Quest 3.
Makna Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Makna Gloves are light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is part of the Makna set of armour along with the Makna Cap, Makna Top, Makna Bottoms and Makna Shoes.

Maguel Road (Japanese: , Mākuueru Kaidō) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of Bionis' Leg, east of Raguel Bridge. It leads up to the upper level. Some Mechon can be found on the road.

Magnum Charge (Japanese: , Baretto Chāji, Bullet Charge) is one of Reyn's support arts in . When activated, the damage from the next physical art used will be increased significantly. In order to use this art, Reyn's talent gauge must be full. In , Nene has an identical version of this art called Magnum Starch.

Marble Krabbles are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are a type of Krabble that can be found at Hazzai Cape in Colony 9. They are found at levels 7-12. They can drop Small Shells, which are required for Material Quest 1.

Marcia's Biscuits is a Key Item in . It is given to the party by Marcia in two different quests. During Biscuits for a Grandson they are to be delivered to her grandson Jiroque, and during Thawing Relations they are to be delivered to Zukazu. The descriptions imply that she did not take the time to bake a fresh batch for Zukazu.

Magnis Arduns (Japanese: , Magunisu Arudon) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Ardun family, and can be found on Bionis' Leg. They often appear in pairs and are usually both level 77. They are the only source of Ardun Elder Beards, which are needed for the reconstruction of Colony 6 and for Replica Monado 1. As soon as they see the party and attack they will almost always use "Armu Plough", an extremely strong physical attack, and will most likely kill the party if they have just reached Bionis' Leg in the story. They can be found near Rho Oasis and to the south of the Jabos Rock Rest Area, near the end of Bionis' Leg.

The Machina Refuge (Japanese: , Mashīna no Kakurega) is a Secret Area in . It is a hidden room located on the fourth floor of Mechonis Field. There are five Machina at this location, one of whom is Bozatrox. The Machina Refuge Shop is also located here. To get to the Machina Refuge, the party must traverse the last platform of the Great Battle Scar. This can be accomplished by warping to the Great Battle Scar, and taking the vent upwards. Once at the top, instead of going left to get to the interior, if the party heads right, they will come to a bend that dead-ends at a long slope downwards. The party needs to slide down the slope to the first landing and then the second and climb the ladder
Mani Defenders (Japanese: , Izayoi no Gotō, Guard Sword of the Sixteenth Night) are weapons in . They are swords wielded by Dunban.

Maleza Kromars are minor enemies in . They are members of the Kromar family. They can be found in the Eryth Sea on Hovering Reef 6, 7, and 8. Five of them must be defeated to complete Eryth Sea's Monster Quest 2.

M85 Meteor Artillery (Japanese: , Hachijūgoshiki Ryūseitsutsu-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and two of them can be found at level 57 on the Fallen Arm, around the Connecting Bridge. Defeating three of them is required to complete the quest Protect the Village given by Eleqa in the Hidden Machina Village. They drop Refined Part Ls, ten of which are needed for Broken Ether Furnace.

M56 Prototypes (Japanese: , Gojūrokushiki: PROTO) are Mechon enemies in . They can be found at level 54 on the Digit 5 beach and in Digit 1 Crevasse on the Fallen Arm. Defeating ten of them is required to complete the quest Stop the Mechon Rampage! given by Eleqa in the Hidden Machina Village. They drop Dated Frames, two of which are required for Fixing a Broken Door.

Machina Driver IIIs (Japanese: , Makina Bankā 3) are unique weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn, and can only be acquired as a reward for one quest or dropped by Mechon in Agniratha and the Central Factory.
Machina Guarders IIIs (Japanese: , Makina Gādā 3) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn, and can be acquired both from a shop and dropped by a variety of Mechon.
Machina Drivers II (Japanese: , Makina Bankā 2) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn.
Machina Drivers (Japanese: , Makina Bankā) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn.
The Machina Guarder (Japanese: , Makina Gādā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.
A Marble Driver (Japanese: , Māburubankā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.
The Machina Sword III (Japanese: , Makina Sōdo 3) is a unique weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is an Anti-Mechon sword wielded by Dunban, and can only be dropped by four Mechon.
Machina Blade IIs (Japanese: , Makina Burēdo 2) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are swords wielded by Dunban.
Machina Blade IIIs (Japanese: , Makina Burēdo 3) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are swords wielded by Dunban. They can be purchased at Hidden Village Shop 1 for 38,400 G

Machina Sword IIs (Japanese: , Makina Sōdo 2) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon-damaging swords wielded by Dunban. When sheathed, the weapon looks like a bronze or brass-coloured hilt shaped to resemble a miniature Monado, but once Dunban draws it for battle, the weapon emits a blue blade, not unlike the one from the Monado.
Machina Blades (Japanese: , Makina Burēdo) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are swords wielded by Dunban.
The Machina Sword (Japanese: , Makina Sōdo) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a sword wielded by Dunban.

The Machina Rifle III (Japanese: , Makina Raifuru 3) is a unique weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is Sharla's strongest Anti-Mechon ether rifle, although its built-in gems are potentially less useful than the built-in gems in the Machina Rifle II. The Machina Rifle III can only be dropped by a small number of Mechon in the Central Factory and Agniratha.
Machina Snipers II (Japanese: , Makina Sunaipu 2) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are ether rifles wielded by Sharla.
The Machina Rifle II (Japanese: , Makina Raifuru 2) is one of Sharla's Ether Rifles. It is one of her few weapons that can damage Mechon.
The Machina Nibbler III (Japanese: , Makina Bakubaku 3) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a biter wielded by Riki, and is one of his strongest weapons capable of damaging the Mechon.
The Machina Biter II (Japanese: , Makina Kamukamu 2) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a biter wielded by Riki, and can damage Mechon.

Machina Biters (Japanese: , Makina Kamukamu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters that can be wielded by Riki. They can be acquired by trading with Ewan in the Refugee Camp as well as purchasing it at Hidden Village Shop 1 on Fallen Arm for 28,320 G.

Machina Staff III (Japanese: , Makina Sutaffu 3) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are staves that can be wielded by Melia. They can be obtained by purchasing it at the Hidden Village Shop 1 in Fallen Arm after the events at the Meyneth Shrine for 33,600 G.

The Machina Staff II (Japanese: , Makina Sutaffu 2) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a staff that can be wielded by Melia. It can be obtained by purchasing it at the Central Tower Shop in Agniratha for 27,600 G.
Machina Staves (Japanese: , Makina Sutaffu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are staves wielded by Melia. They can only be obtained via purchase at the Hidden Village Shop 1 for 25,800 G.
Machina Rods (Japanese: , Makina Roddo) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are staves that can be wielded by Melia.

Makna Piranhax (Japanese: , Makuna Samon) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Piranhax family, and can be found in packs at level 30 around the Clear Waterfall in Makna Forest. They drop Piranhax Belly Meat, five of which are required for the quest Even In the Chief's Absence.

Magestic Mordred (Japanese: , Ōjō no Morudoreddo) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Fortress-type Mechon that can be found at level 70 on the third floor of Central Factory, northeast from the Face Maintenance Bay.

Makna Feris (Japanese: , Makuna Ferisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Feris family, and can be found at level 31 in Makna Forest, primarily between the Waypoint Beacon and the Nopon Arch. They can also be found near the Sparkling Pool. Two must be defeated for the quest Monster Quest 2. They can drop Feris Blood, which is needed for Losing the Taste for Alcohol.

Makna Water is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found at the base of Great Makna Falls, directly west of the Divine Sanctuary in Makna Forest. This item is required for Preparing for Adventure.
Mana Chunks are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Arel, Aora, and Asara Telethia in either Eryth Sea or Alcamoth. Mana Chunks are not available for trade.

Makna Brogs (Japanese: , Makuna Guroggu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Brog family, and can be found at level 33 in the pool south of the Nopon Arch in Makna Forest. They can also be found on the shores of the river connected to the Great Makna Falls, below the various bridges. They are the only enemies that drop Bloody Brog Sweat, two lots of which are needed for World's Strongest Flavour.
Mag Storm (Japanese: , Bagu Sutōmu) is one of Fiora's Ether arts in . It hits all enemies within 15 meters. It also inflicts Daze on Toppled Mechon.

Mad Upas (Japanese: , Maddo Ūpā) are enemies in . They are members of the Upa family, and can be found at levels 23-25 in Satorl Marsh. They can be found northeast of Exile Fortress and west of Glowing Obelisk. They can drop the Glowing Upa Seeds needed for Making Camp.

A Mammut (Japanese: , Mamūto) is a type of quadrupedal dinosaur-like enemy in the . They are very uncommon and tend to live in the same areas as Sauros. Mammuts resemble triceratops dinosaurs and elephants (hence the name coming from Mammoth) and all have the same appearance. Behemoths closely resemble Mammuts.

The M88 Watchtower (Japanese: , Hachijūhachishiki Kanshitōki) is a story exclusive and quest exclusive Mechon enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found at level 62 in the Central Factory near the Main Factory Gate. It only appears during Materials for a Bomb, and drops the Electrical Fuse required to complete that quest. It will also drop a Reinforced Plunger, which can be used to complete Best Boots.

The M97 Commander (Japanese: , Kyūjūnanashiki Butaichōki) is a story exclusive and quest exclusive Mechon enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is not a Unique Monster. It can be found at level 64 in Central Factory in the Large Mechon Store. It only appears during the quest Materials for a Bomb, and drops the Ether Explosive required to complete Materials for a Bomb. It can drop the Reinforced Thrusters needed for A Weapon Just For Me.

M42 Scout Units (Japanese: , Yonjūnishiki: Teisatsugata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 13 near Raguel Bridge - South and Maguel Road on Bionis' Leg. M42 Scout Units also appear in the Ether Mine, where they are level 19 and drop different items.
Makna Antols (Japanese: , Makuna Antoru) are enemies in . They are members of the Antol family, and can be found at levels 40-43 in King Agni's Tomb, in Makna Forest.
M46 Covert Killers (Japanese: , Yonjūrokushiki Kurōto-gata: Tei) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 46 in Dolgan Outpost and Enalda Control Base in Sword Valley.

M54 Armoured Units (Japanese: , Gojūyonshiki Ryōsōki-gata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 47 in Sword Valley at the 3rd Gate, between the 4th Gate and 5th Gate, at Dolgan Outpost, and at the Monado Wound.

M63X Android Units (Japanese: , Rokujūsanshiki Kairyōjin-gata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 48 in Sword Valley between the 3rd Gate and 4th Gate, between the 4th and 5th Gates, at the 6th Gate, at the Enalda Control Base, and at the Ether Storage Area.
M54 Attack Units (Japanese: , Gojūyonshiki Kōkō-gata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 49 in Sword Valley at the Radio Tower.

M63 Harvester Units (Japanese: , Rokujūsanshiki Jinshokukai-gata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 49 in Sword Valley at the 3rd Gate, between the 3rd and 4th Gates, at the Enalda Control Base, and at the Ether Storage Area.

M82 Melee Units (Japanese: , Hachijūnishiki Hakuhei Ōgata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 50 in Sword Valley between the 3rd Gate and 4th Gate, at Enalda Control Base, the Ether Storage Area, and the Port Maintenance Bay.

M63 Destruction Units (Japanese: , Rokujūsanshiki Hakai-gata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 50 in Sword Valley at the Control Tower, the Port Access Pathway, and the Port Maintenance Bay.
M71 Flexible Units (Japanese: , Nanajūichishiki Jūnankai-gata) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 49 - 50 near the Ether Storage Area in Sword Valley.

M82X Melee Units (Japanese: , Hachijūnishiki Hakuhei Ōgata Kai) are Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 50 - 52 in Sword Valley, along the lower path between the Heavy Machine Depot and the Radio Tower.

M58 Tactical Units (Japanese: , Gojūhachishiki Sōhei-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in the Main Maintenance Bay and the Ether Input Stream in Galahad Fortress.

M66 Supply Units (Japanese: , Rokujūrokushiki Hokyū-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in Galahad Fortress in the 1st Fuel Supply Room, 2nd Fuel Supply Room, and 3rd Fuel Supply Room. They can drop the Refined Part Ms needed for Restoring the Capital 2. However, by the time the quest is available, they cannot be defeated anymore.

M66 Production Units (Japanese: , Rokujūrokushiki Renpei-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in Galahad Fortress in the Ether Input Stream. They can drop the Refined Part Ms needed for Restoring the Capital 2. However, by the time the quest is available, they cannot be defeated anymore.

M48 Sentry Units (Japanese: , Yonjūhachishiki Shuyōsai-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in Galahad Fortress in the Blast Furnace Conduit and the Ether Input Stream.

M65 Hunter Units (Japanese: , Rokujūgoshiki Sōtō-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in the Main Maintenance Bay, the 2nd Turbine Room, and in the passages near the Ether Input Stream in Galahad Fortress. They can drop the Refined Part Ms needed for Restoring the Capital 2. However, by the time the quest is available, they cannot be defeated anymore.

M59 Captains (Japanese: , Gojūkyūshiki Butaichō-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in the Main Maintenance Bay and the Ether Input Stream in Galahad Fortress.

M68 Construction Units (Japanese: , Rokujūhachishiki Kōsakujūshi-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in the Main Maintenance Bay in Galahad Fortress. They can drop the Refined Part Ms needed for Restoring the Capital 2. However, by the time the quest is available, they cannot be defeated anymore.

M85 Infantry Units (Japanese: , Hachijūgoshiki Seikihei-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in Galahad Fortress in the Ether Input Stream. They can drop the Refined Part Ls needed for Broken Ether Furnace. However, by the time this quest in accepted, it is impossible to defeat them anymore.

M85 Sergeants (Japanese: , Hachijūgoshiki Shōtaichō-gata) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found in the Ether Blast Furnace in Galahad Fortress. They can drop the Refined Part Ls needed for Broken Ether Furnace. However, by the time this quest in accepted, it is impossible to defeat them anymore.
M87 Prototypes (Japanese: , Hachijūnanashiki: PROTO) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found at level 55 near the Black Wreckage on the Fallen Arm.
Machina Energy is a Key Item in . It is needed for Lifespan of a Machina and it only spawns once this quest has been accepted. It can be found at the Mechon Wreckage Site in Colony 9.

The M71 Fire Support (Japanese: , Chōkaryoku Nanajūichishiki Kishinhei) is a quest exclusive Mechon enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found at the Freight Elevator outside Colony 6 only during the quest Defend Colony 6 - Elite. Defeating it is required to complete the quest.

The M94 Guard Unit is a story exclusive and quest exclusive Mechon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found at level 54 at Face Maintenance Bay in Galahad Fortress during the story event and quest Fiora's Conviction. It is defending Face Nemesis along with another variant, one Defensive Guard Unit and its variant. It has 129,000 HP, and while it does not respawn or drop a Treasure Chest.

The M83 Predator Unit (Japanese: , Hachijūsanshiki Hoshoku-gata) is a story exclusive Mechon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found at level 51 at Ulna Passage on the Fallen Arm. It appears along with two M54 Slayer Units during a story event battle against Shulk protecting Fiora after the party drops from Galahad Fortress to the Fallen Arm. It does not carry any items or drop any chests.

M54 Slayer Units (Japanese: , Gojūyonshiki Tsukigiri-gata) are two story exclusive Mechon in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found at level 50 at Ulna Passage on the Fallen Arm. They appear along with the M83 Predator Unit during a story event battle against Shulk protecting Fiora after the party drops from Galahad Fortress to the Fallen Arm. They do not carry any items or drop any chests.

Mad Taunt (Japanese: , Maddo Taunto) is Reyn's Talent Art in . It generates a large amount of provocation aggro to the targeted enemy. This aggro dissipates at a rate of 1/30 of the original amount per second, reaching zero after 30 seconds. In , Nene has an identical version of this art called Glad Taunt.

Mammut Horns are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Laeklit Mammuts in Makna Forest, and are not available for trade. According to their description, they come from the king of fierce monsters and they will not break under any attack. One of them is needed for the quest Replica Monado 4.

Maintenance Wing Escape (Japanese: , Seibitō wo Nukero) is a Story Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received automatically at the Maintenance Wing in Central Factory while progressing in the upper level where is located the room with the Barrier Control Panel. Upon completing this quest, two Offensive/FOUNDs and three M57/BEASTs appear, blocking the path to the lift. Defeating them is not explicitly required, but may be necessary if the party cannot sneak past them. Once they are defeated they will not respawn.

The Main Maintenance Bay (Japanese: , Chūō Seibishitsu) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of Galahad Fortress. There is an Earth Ether Gear here, as well as a lift to a lower floor (requiring the Fortress Pass Key to activate). There are three rooms joining the bay - the 1st Fuel Supply Room, 2nd Fuel Supply Room and 3rd Fuel Supply Room. It is most likely a place for damaged Mechon to be repaired in the fortress.

The Main Factory Gate (Japanese: , Seisan Kōjō Shōmen Gēto) is a location in . It is located on the second floor of the Central Factory. The M88 Watchtower, who drops the Electrical Fuse needed for Materials for a Bomb, can be found here.

Maintenance Entrance 1 (Japanese: , Seibi-tō Dai-1 Han'nyūguchi) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of the Central Factory, near the Control Tower. This location is the subject of To the Central Tower.

The Maintenance Wing (Japanese: , Kishinpei Seibi-tō) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of the Central Factory. The Weapon Creation Panel, which is needed for the quest Find a Path to the Top and New Weapon for Fiora can be found here.

The Main Control Room (Japanese: , Ēteru Yōkōro Kanseishitsu) is a landmark in . It is located on the first basement floor of Galahad Fortress, and connects the 1st Turbine Room and the 2nd Turbine Room.
Mana Fragments are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Asha and Polkan Telethia in Colony 6.

Marcus (Japanese: , Mākasu; English dub: ) is an NPC in . He can be found at the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District during the day, talking to Irina and two unnamed BLADE members. Marcus is a member of the Interceptors Division.

Majesty (雄大, Grandeur) is an Event Track in , composed and arranged by ACE+. It is track 16 of disc 1 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack, and track five of disc two from the Xenoblade Definitive Edition Original Soundtrack and the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This music is a somber but grand theme that is heard during the cutscene when Shulk and Reyn marvel at the view of the Bionis and Mechonis from Kneecap Hill upon emerging from Tephra Cave, and later at the end of the game when Shulk deals the final blow to Zanza in order that he and his friends might seize their destiny and save their world. In , this song plays during the cutscene following the first phase of the fina

MNN＋@0・ is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track nine of disc three from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. This music is heard while the party is in the Ma-non Ship. It also plays during the party's first encounters with the Ma-non and with the Orpheans.
The Machina Refuge Shop is a shop in . It is located in Mechonis Field. It is a good and easy source for strong Anti-Mechon Weapons. This shop is accessible until the events at Meyneth Shrine.

Marnuck Soldiers (Japanese: , Marunāku Sorujā) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion, and can be found at level 30 and 31 at Qing Long Glade then at Shark's Jaws in Noctilum. Seven of them must be defeated over the course of the Affinity Mission Manhunt. Two are fought in Qing Long Glade, while five are fought alongside the Marnuck Commander in the Shark's Jaws.

Manhunt (Japanese: , Dagan to Rīzu no Tsuiseki, The Chase for Dagahn and Ryyz) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be received from Vandham at BLADE Tower in New Los Angeles. The party must save Celica and Rock from the Ganglion. This mission is required in order to unlock Chapter 10.

The Marnuck Commander (Japanese: , Marunāku Komandā) is a mission exclusive enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Marnuck Ganglion, and can be found at level 34 at the Shark's Jaws in Noctilum. He is accompanied by five Marnuck Soldiers. He is involved in the Manhunt Affinity Mission and must be defeated.
Magnum Edge is a Debuff Battle Art in It inficts Physical Res Down.

The Marnucks (マルナーク, Marunāku) are a race of beings in . They are very aggressive warlike alien race and members of the Ganglion coalition. Following Void's return, the Marnuck remained loyal to him, and migrated to Volitaris for the final battle against New Los Angeles's forces. After Mira's complete destruction from the Dematerialization events caused by the Ghosts, it is likely that the Marnuck race has become extinct.

Marnuck Rooks (Japanese: , Marunāku Rūku) are two story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnucks and are fought at level 16 in Sunlit Spring in Noctilum during Chapter 4, where they provide assistance to Goetia during the boss battle.

Marnuck Vanguards (Japanese: , Marunāku Bangādo) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnucks and can be found at level 21-22 at Cliffside Camp or level 28-30 in Sea Whisper Valley in Oblivia.

Mamma Mia! (Japanese: , Mīa no Shuttatsu) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Mia, who is found on a platform in the northwestern outskirts of the Administrative District. It is the first of five missions that ultimately unlock Mia as a recruitable character.
The Marnuck Crafter (Japanese: , Marunāku Kurafuto) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Marnuck and is fought at level 12 on Aaroy Plain in Oblivia during Foggy Dilemma.

Marnuck Analysts (Japanese: , Marunāku Anarishisu) are two Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Marnucks. They are fought at level 12 on Aaroy Plain in Oblivia during Foggy Dilemma.

Marine Lophids (Japanese: , Marīn Rofiru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Lophid family, and can be found at level 52-57 at Cliffside Beach and FN Site 111 in Primordia during the day.
Marnuck Convergers (Japanese: , Marunāku Konbāji) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 51-60 in Jair Fortress in Oblivia.

The Marnuck Quartermasters (Japanese: , Marunāku Kwōtā) are two Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion, and are fought at level 24 at Suncatch Ravine in Noctilum during Rescue at the Ensconced Citadel.

The Marnuck Troopers (Japanese: , Marunāku Torūpā) are four Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and are fought at level 24-26 in Noctilum's Suncatch Ravine during Rescue at the Ensconced Citadel, immediately after the Marnuck Quartermasters are defeated.
Marnuck Minors (Japanese: , Marunāku Mainā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion, and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros's Wildcat Fortress.
Marnuck Shield Troopers (Japanese: , Marunāku Shīrudā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion, and can be found at level 21-30 at the Ruins on the Sandbank in Oblivia.
Malyteth is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at the Cathedral in the Residential District of New Los Angeles during the night.

Machine Queen Quos (Japanese: , Mashīnkuīn Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos and can be found at level 41-43 at Lesser Anvil, Samuel Incline, the west end of the broken land bridge by FN Site 412, the base northwest of FN Site 415, a ravine north of FN Site 416, Sylvalum Searoad, and Badr Stronghold in Sylvalum.

Machine King Quos (Japanese: , Mashīnkingu Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos and can be found at level 51, level 55, level 57, or level 59 in Sylvalum, around North Cinderdunes, Anvil Rocks One and Two, Banshee Cave, above Badr Stronghold, Cavernous Abyss, and Abyss Reservoir.

Malicious Mephites (Japanese: , Marishiasu Mepitesu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mephite family, and can be found at level 33-35 in Noctilum, in the Shark's Jaws northeast of FN Site 210.
Madness Hornets (Japanese: , Maddonesuhōnetto) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.
Madame Mantises (Japanese: , Madamukamakiri) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.
Magus Papils (Japanese: , Meigasu Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 51 in east Lake Ciel in Sylvalum at daytime.

Magus Blattas (Japanese: , Meigasu Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 42-48 on top of a pilar south of FN Site 211 and in the entrance tunnel to the Vitriol Cesspool in Noctilum.
Marbled Suid Fillets are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Suids. One is needed for Cooking Schooled.

Marnuck Recons (Japanese: , Marunāku Sukautā) are Marnuck Ganglion enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Two of them can be found at level 20 guarding FN Site 220 in Noctilum, along with a Marnuck Support a short distance away with whom they share Group Loyalty. They will only appear if a Data Probe has not yet been installed at FN Site 220; when a probe is installed, they will permanently vanish. Another pair can be found just south of Decapotamon Vista.

Marnuck Support (Japanese: , Marunāku Eidā) is a Marnuck Ganglion enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. One can be found at level 20 at Lotus Keep Building Site in Noctilum. Another can be found with a pair of Marnuck Recons at FN Site 220 if a Data Probe has not yet been installed at that site; when a probe is installed, this group permanently vanishes.
Manuelita, the Affectionate (Japanese: , Jiai no Manuerita) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Suid family. It can be found at level 47 in Noctilum at Middle Hushflood.

Man'an, the Water Whisperer (Japanese: , Reisui no Man'an) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Arenatect family. It can be found at level 43 northeast of Lake Ciel in Sylvalum, where it walks to the lake's edge upon spawning. It is accompanied by two Cerulean Arenatects.
Macho Armored Suids (Japanese: , Matcho Āmā Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 51-60 at Scabland Fortress in Oblivia.

Malium Petramands (Japanese: , Mariumu Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family, and can be found at level 51-53 in East Ibra Ravine in Oblivia. Eight of them must be defeated during Petramand Patrol.

Macabre Aeviters (Japanese: , Semetarī Tidāra, Cemetary Aeviter) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Aeviter family, and can be found at level 51-70 in Sandsprint Cavity in Sylvalum. Two level 60 Macabre Aeviters are dormant next to Berthold, the Blue-Eyed. There are also two active level 66 Macabre Aeviters, they spawn near the entrance after a while after walking further into the cave, and are the only Aeviters in the game that walk around normally after spawning rather than lying in wait.
Macabre Gerrids (Japanese: , Semetarī Girafa) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Gerrid family, and can be found at level 31-40 in Den of the Dead in Sylvalum.
Marnuck Admirals (Japanese: , Marunāku Adomiraru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 at Bedrock Hold in Primordia.

Marnuck Aspirers (Japanese: , Marunāku Anbishasu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 in Cauldros's Boxtrap Checkpoint or O'rrh Sim Gate. Six must be defeated for Marnuck Masher.
Marnuck Barragers (Japanese: , Marunāku Baretto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 21-30 in Cauldros, near FN Site 502.
Marnuck Blasters (Japanese: , Marunāku Burasutā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 in Cauldros, near FN Site 502.
Marnuck Bursters (Japanese: , Marunāku Bāsuto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 51 on Anvil Rock One, southwest of FN Site 415 in Sylvalum.
Marnuck Crashers (Japanese: , Marunāku Inpakuto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Oblivia's Scabland Fortress.
Marnuck Cutthroats (Japanese: , Marunāku Anfea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 at the west end of Oblivia's Big Arch.
Marnuck Damagers (Japanese: , Marunāku Hāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Oblivia's Scabland Fortress.
Marnuck Dynamos (Japanese: , Marunāku Fōsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 51-60 in Cauldros's Bestial Utopia or Ganglion Antropolis.

Marnuck Evildoers (Japanese: , Marunāku Wikeddo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 34-36 at FN Site 416, South Hardheart Canyon, and Hilal Stronghold in Sylvalum.

Marnuck Firetroopers (Japanese: , Marunāku Furea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 42-50 in Badr Stronghold, the Anvil Rocks, and on the Sylvalum Searoad (near the Lifehold Unit) in Sylvalum.

Marnuck Gatlings (Japanese: , Marunāku Riborubu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 51-60 in Cauldros's Old Ceremonial Hollow or at the Ganglion Antropolis.
Marnuck Grapplers (Japanese: , Marunāku Gurappurā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 in Cauldros's Boxtrap Checkpoint.
Marnuck Guardians (Japanese: , Marunāku Gādian) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 in Oblivia, north of FN Site 309.
Marnuck Hornets (Japanese: , Marunāku Hōnetto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros, near FN Site 511.
Marnuck Howitzers (Japanese: , Marunāku Hauzā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Oblivia's Scabland Fortress.
Marnuck Imperials (Japanese: , Marunāku Inperiaru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros's O'rrh Sim Gate or O'rrh Sim Keep.
Marnuck Jaegers (Japanese: , Marunāku Yēgā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Primordia, near FN Site 101 or FN Site 119.
Marnuck Marksmen (Japanese: , Marunāku Mākusuman) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 21-30 in Primordia, west of FN Site 108.
Marnuck Mercenaries (Japanese: , Marunāku Māsenarī) are enemies in . They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 at the Milligan Supply Base in Oblivia.
Marnuck Pawns (Japanese: , Marunāku Pōn) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 1-10 in Cauldros, on the Far Isle of Tzu'o.

Marnuck Pulsers (Japanese: , Marunāku Parusā) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 51-60 in Cauldros. They can be found in the Old Ceremonial Hollow, to name one specific.

Marnuck Sentinels (Japanese: , Marunāku Senchineru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 at night accompanying Daril, the Eradicator, on the edge of the pond near the entrance to Primordia's Castaway Cavern.

Marnuck Slayers (Japanese: , Marunāku Deddorī) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 59 at Cavernous Abyss in Sylvalum. They are on a ledge above the western side of the abyss. During the day Ahama, the Covetous appears on the same ledge. At night Badul's Seidr appears there.
Marnuck Sluggers (Japanese: , Marunāku Suraggā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros's Wildcat Fortress.
Marnuck Transitioners (Japanese: , Marunāku Toranjishon) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros, norhtwest of FN Site 511.

Marnuck Windtroopers (Japanese: , Marunāku Geiru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 31-40 at night accompanying Daril, the Eradicator, on the edge of the pond near the entrance to Primordia's Castaway Cavern.
MO037: Moore (Japanese: , MO037: Moa) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Definian who appears in Cauldros, where the party battles her.

The Major Chimera (Japanese: , Mejā Kimaera) is a Story Exclusive Secondary Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Chimera family, and is fought at level 49 inside the Lifehold Core during Chapter 12. It can assist, along with the Mezzo or the Minor Chimeras, the Queen Chimera summoned by Lao if the fight lasts long. None of these Chimeras are registered in the Enemy Index, except Lao as well as the Soldier Chimeras from the previous battle.
Marine Rutiles are Precious Resources in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are components of many Rank XX augments.

The Gunner Marnuck (Japanese: , Gannā Marunāku) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Marnuck Ganglion and appears at level 35 at the Bedrock Hold in Primordia. Defeating it is required during the Affinity Mission Blitzkrieg.
Machine Gunner is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Bastion Warrior at rank 2. Cross, Lin, Frye, and Nagi can use this skill.
MG062: Megisia is a Definian in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is the older sister of MG068: Megisia. In battle she pilots a Galdr which shares her name.
MG068: Megisia is a Definian in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is the younger sister of MG062: Megisia. In battle she pilots a Seidr which shares her name.

Magna Galdr (Japanese: , Maguna Garudora) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Galdr machines, Ganglion's vehicles, and can be found at level 64 above Anvil Sandplain in Sylvalum, above Luxaar's Xern.

Mach Shrads (Japanese: , Mahha Zuttā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Shrad machines, and can be found at level 51-60 in Cauldros, on the bridges above and to the east of Capital Wreckage. They sometimes roll off the edge of the bridge, or may be knocked off the bridge during a battle.

Marnuck Scouts (Japanese: , Marunāku Sukauto) are three Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Marnucks fought at level 37 at T'phnom Shelf in Cauldros during Until the End.
The Hunter Kit is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained from Capsica and is needed to complete Trade Agreement.
Man'celeg is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is an Orphean.
Mamara (English dub: ) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Nopon and can be found at the Dorian Caravan in Oblivia during Mia Grows Up.

Malevolent Petramand Silks are materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Petramands in Cauldros. Six of them are needed during My Angel, My Lana. They are also needed to engineer rank X, XV, and XX Ranged Appendage Damage and Crush.APPEND Augments.
Malyteth's Bottle is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It's obtained from Malyteth at Biahno Water-Purification Plant in Primordia after she attempts to drink it during The Miracle Maker.
Marnuck Masher is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Drongo Caravan to defeat Marnuck Aspirers in Cauldros.

Maneater is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles, between Irina and Cross. The dialogue is different depending on whether Cross is male or female
